A1.justification: Both complete PDFs describe the same AnomalyNCD work, with readable text, equations, tables and figures. V1's main-text analyses can be matched to v2's main text and Appendices A-P.

before.justification: V1 reports original AnomalyNCD experiments on MVTec AD and MTD, including benchmark comparisons and component ablations in Tables I-X.

after.justification: V2 retains those experiments and adds empirical analyses of labeled-data choice, parameter sensitivity, inference time and failure cases.

M1.justification: V2 Section 3.2 selects the most frequent nonzero count of connected regions for MEBin; v1 Section III-B selects the most frequent count without excluding zero. This changes the stated selection rule when zero dominates. The architecture, training losses, cropping and region-merging procedure otherwise remain equivalent.

E1.justification: Both versions use MVTec AD, MTD and AeBAD-S and retain image-level classification, region-level classification, combined-anomaly examples and ideal-mask evaluation. V2's additional rotations of labeled MVTec categories and supervised control alter protocols within existing data and task coverage.

E2.justification: The main benchmark comparator sets are unchanged. V2 adds a supervised ViT comparator to the attention analysis in Figure 10 and introduces explicit t-SNE comparisons against AC and UniFormaly in Figure 15; these comparators were absent from the corresponding qualitative comparisons in v1.

E3.justification: V2 substantially extends evaluation design: 14 MVTec product categories supply labeled training data in turn, a supervised ViT control uses leave-one-out validation, and new experiments sweep MEBin and pseudo-label-correction parameters and measure inference stages. The original benchmark splits, backbone, training budget and primary metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds substantial analyses of dependence on labeled-data choice, supervised attention, threshold sensitivity, computational bottlenecks and EfficientAD failures, alongside expanded binarization and clustering visualizations. Most original ablations survive, including those moved to the appendix. The RD++ binarization-threshold sweep and the t-SNE comparison without labeled data are omitted.

E5.justification: V2 Table 16 newly reports variance across minimum-stable-range parameter settings. This is a sensitivity statistic, not uncertainty across repeated random runs. Neither version supplies repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests for the reported performance.

E6.justification: Main NMI, ARI and F1 scores and the original quantitative ablations are retained, but v2 adds source-choice matrices, parameter sweeps, per-product results and timing: 153.1 ms/image excluding anomaly detection. MuSc's AUPRO entries are omitted. Table 15 reports default-setting MTD PatchCore F1 of 0.715, conflicting with 0.617 retained in Tables 2 and 8; this does not establish a performance gain.

T1.justification: V2 corrects the normal-class target in pseudo-label correction: v1 Equation 4 uses a Cu-dimensional vector despite generating predictions over Cl+Cu classes; v2 Equation 5 defines a compatible Cl+Cu-dimensional vector with its nonzero entry at Cl+1. Other equations are retained or restated, including the training losses moved to Appendix A; no proofs or theorems are added.

C1.justification: The first contribution changes from the first application of NCD to industrial scenarios to the first self-supervised method for multi-class anomaly classification, broadening the stated priority claim. The central framework contributions, benchmark superiority claims and headline gains remain the same.

C2.justification: V2 adds a specific qualification to the relationship between detector quality and classification: EfficientAD can perform poorly despite high AUPRO because anomaly-score scales vary across images, causing missed regions during binarization (Appendix P/Figure 13). It also explains the runtime bottleneck and parameter tradeoffs. Existing interpretations of masks, labeled data and region merging are largely retained.

D1.justification: V2 newly identifies an NVIDIA RTX 3090 for timing and OpenCV connected-component processing without CUDA acceleration. Existing training and cropping details are retained in Appendices B-C. The project code link remains, but the specific unofficial EfficientAD implementation link supplied by v1 is removed.

R1.justification: V2 removes the standalone representation-learning survey and several peripheral references, while adding citations on texture anomaly clustering, masked-attention segmentation and NCD segmentation. The novelty framing changes, but the principal positioning against frozen-feature anomaly clustering and natural-image NCD remains.

P1.justification: The introduction, related work and method narrative are extensively rewritten and condensed. Training details and several existing analyses move into a structured supplement with an overview and Appendices A-P. Terminology changes include MGCRL to MGRL and PLR to PLC. Some appendix citations now appear as unresolved question marks.

P2.justification: V2 redraws the training, MEBin and region-merging diagrams, rearranges attention and t-SNE panels, and adds extensive appendix tables and visual comparisons. Existing tables are relocated and reformatted; one-class AUPRO values move from rows into column headers. The document also adopts a different publication layout and caption style.

improvement.justification: V1 already provides extensive benchmarks and component ablations. V2 adds useful evidence about labeled-data choice, sensitivity, runtime and detector failures, improving practical assessment of the method. The gain is tempered by unresolved appendix citations and the conflicting default-setting F1 in Table 15 versus Tables 2 and 8, which weakens confidence in part of the new sensitivity analysis.
